news_headlines.title: Princess Cruises Introduces Voyager Class, Orders Three Ships
news_headlines.summary: Princess Cruises is launching a new "Voyager Class" with three new ships, to be delivered in late 2035, 2038, and 2039. These vessels, built by Fincantieri, will be the largest in Princess's fleet at 183,000 gross tons each, accommodating approximately 4,700 guests. They will be dual-fuel powered by Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), continuing Carnival Corporation's commitment to more environmentally friendly cruise ships.

news_headlines.title: Three 4,700-guest Princess cruise ships are coming, first in 2035
news_headlines.summary: Princess Cruises, a brand under Carnival Corporation, has signed agreements with Fincantieri for three new Voyager class cruise ships, scheduled for delivery in late 2035, 2038, and 2039. These vessels will each be 183,000 gross tons, accommodate approximately 4,700 guests, and will be dual-fuel LNG-powered to reduce emissions. This order is a significant part of Carnival Corporation's fleet enhancement strategy and will increase its LNG-based fleet to 21 ships, pending financing and customary terms.

news_headlines.title: Arcosa Divests Marine Unit for $450M to Focus on Infrastructure & Engineered Structures - News and Statistics
news_headlines.summary: Arcosa has sold its inland barge business, Arcosa Marine Products Inc., to Wynnchurch Capital for $450 million in cash. This divestiture is part of Arcosa's strategy to reduce operational complexity and cyclical exposure, allowing the company to focus on its higher-margin construction materials and engineered structures divisions, which are expected to benefit from U.S. infrastructure and power market trends. Prior to this sale, Arcosa also acquired a Florida-based aggregates company for $60 million, signaling a continued focus on reinvestment in high-growth segments.
